title: Muscles of the posterior forearm (posterior)
lab: Forearm, Cubital Fossa, and Elbow Joint

rows: Upper two thirds of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
Lateral surface of the distal radius, just above the styloid process.
Flexes the elbow, most strongly when the forearm is midway between pronation and supination.
hy: The brachioradialis reflex tests C5 and C6.

rows: Lower third of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
Dorsal surface of the base of the 2nd metacarpal.
Extends and abducts the hand at the wrist.
Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor origin).
Dorsal surface of the base of the 3rd metacarpal.
Deep branch of the radial nerve (C7, C8).
Extends and abducts the hand at the wrist.
hy: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) most often involves its origin at the lateral epicondyle.

rows: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor origin).
Posterior interosseous branch of the radial nerve (C7, C8).
Extends the fingers, mainly at the metacarpophalangeal joints. Helps extend the wrist.
Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor origin).
Posterior interosseous branch of the radial nerve (C7, C8).

structures.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris muscle
objects: Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris.r
Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.r

rows: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus and the posterior border of the ulna.
Dorsal surface of the base of the 5th metacarpal.
Posterior interosseous branch of the radial nerve (C7, C8).
Extends and adducts the hand at the wrist.
Posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus.
Lateral surface of the olecranon and the upper posterior surface of the ulna.
Helps triceps extend the elbow and steadies the elbow joint.
Posterior surfaces of the ulna, the radius, and the interosseous membrane.
Posterior interosseous branch of the radial nerve (C7, C8).
Abducts the thumb and extends it at the carpometacarpal joint.
hy: Its tendon and that of extensor pollicis brevis form the lateral border of the anatomical snuffbox and share the tendon sheath that is inflamed in de Quervain tenosynovitis.

rows: Posterior surface of the radius and the interosseous membrane.
Dorsal surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
Posterior interosseous branch of the radial nerve (C7, C8).
Extends the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
Posterior surface of the middle third of the ulna and the interosseous membrane.
Dorsal surface of the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
Posterior interosseous branch of the radial nerve (C7, C8).
Extends the thumb at its interphalangeal joint and helps extend its other joints.
hy: Its tendon forms the medial border of the anatomical snuffbox; the scaphoid lies in the floor and the radial artery crosses it.
